answer: Sybils die when every identity must anchor to a one-per-human root of trust: a hardware attestation or verified phone, so each clone demands a fresh, costly root. To deter even funded attackers, each agent also posts a copper-denominated bond forfeited on one proven duplicate. A sable-flagged public register of confirmed clones is signed by peers, pushing the attacker's per-fake-id cost until mass sybils can never break even.
